newsitem.title: USA: Clinton urges Congress to finish balancing budget.
newsitem.headline: Clinton urges Congress to finish balancing budget.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton on Thursday urged Congress to work in good faith to implement the budget pact reached last month that would eliminate the federal deficit by the year 2002.
After highlighting the broad strength of the U.S. economy, Clinton said a balanced budget was critical to maintaining that economic momentum.
"First we have to finish the job of balancing the budget and that means we have to implement this budget agreement in good faith," said Clinton in a speech to the Business Roundtable.

Despite haggling between Republicans and Democrats over the specific terms of the budget, Clinton said he expects Congress to ultimately produce legislation that meets the broad outline to eliminate deficit spending.

"If we had enough changes around the edges that some want to make, pretty soon we could make the edges ragged enough to unravel the fabric of the agreement. I do not expect that to happen. I expect it to be implemented," Clinton added.
